publications.title: DRSP supervisory responsibilities remain unchanged following ESMA assessment
publications.summary: DRSP supervisory responsibilities remain unchanged following ESMA assessment 18 November 2026 Market data Supervision The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has finalised its annual assessment of the derogation criteria for Data Reporting Services Providers (DRSPs) . ESMA’s supervisory responsibilities for DRSPs will remain unchanged, as the ten DRSPs currently supervised by ESMA continue to exceed the relevant derogation thresholds, while the derogated DRSPs remain under the supervision of their respective national competent authorities (NCAs). The assessment is based on data from the 2025 calendar year. Next steps Following the notification of the outcome of the assessment, ESMA will continue to monitor developments and engage with NCAs and supervised entities to ensure a smooth and transparent supervisory process. publications.title: Helping more people break the cycle of persistent credit card debt
publications.summary: Credit cards are a useful financial tool for many – offering flexibility and helping people manage spending and cash flow.But if customers only make low repayments over a long period, they can end up in debt for years while racking up interest and charges.The persistent debt rules we introduced in 2018 aimed to tackle this.They said that lenders had to identify customers who, over an 18-month period, paid more in interest, fees and charges than towards their balance.Lenders had to contact these customers and encourage them to increase repayments if they could afford it, and if they were still struggling, lenders had to take additional steps to help them repay their balances sustainably.What changed for consumersOur evaluation shows that consumer outcomes improved between 2018 and early 2023. publications.title: FINMA adopts measures aimed at relieving the burden on supervised institutions
publications.summary: The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA is continuing to develop its supervisory and licensing processes. It aims to reduce the administrative burden on supervised institutions, simplify processes and focus its resources even more effectively on key risks. At the forefront are more efficient licensing procedures, including a fast track for particularly well-prepared applications with low-risk business models in the FinTech sector. In addition, FINMA is optimising its supervisory processes and data collection and will, in future, consult the relevant sector before publishing key guidance. It is contributing further proposals for simplifying financial market regulation to the work of the Federal Department of Finance (FDF).
